title: When I was little: the imparfait
topic: formation and uses of the imparfait
why: This lesson opens the unit on memories with the imparfait, the second past tense of French, used for habits, descriptions, age and weather in the past. It's the easiest tense to form, and it lets you talk about your childhood before learning, next time, how to combine it with the passé composé.

A second past tense: the imparfait

The passé composé tells what happened. But to talk about your childhood, describe a house or say what you used to do, French uses a second past tense: the imparfait. Good news: it's the most regular tense in French.

How to build it

Take the nous form of the present, remove -ons, and add the endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.

Infinitivenous formStemje form
parlernous parlonsparl-je parlais
finirnous finissonsfiniss-je finissais
prendrenous prenonspren-je prenais
fairenous faisonsfais-je faisais
avoirnous avonsav-j'avais
allernous allonsall-j'allais
parlerfinirêtre
je / j'je parlaisje finissaisj'étais
tutu parlaistu finissaistu étais
il / elle / onil parlaitelle finissaiton était
nousnous parlionsnous finissionsnous étions
vousvous parliezvous finissiezvous étiez
ils / ellesils parlaientelles finissaientils étaient

Only être is irregular, with the stem ét-. The endings are the same for every verb. And -ais, -ait and -aient all sound the same, like the è of mère: je parlais, il parlait and ils parlaient are identical to the ear.

Spelling-change verbs keep the sound of the present: je mangeais (with an e, to keep the soft g), je commençais (with ç). But before -ions and -iez, no need: nous mangions, nous commencions.

", "

What the imparfait is for

1. Habits in the past

What you did regularly, over and over: English says \"used to\" or \"would\".

Quand j'étais petit, je jouais dans la rue.When I was little, I used to play in the street.
Le mercredi, j'allais chez ma grand-mère.On Wednesdays, I would go to my grandmother's.

2. Descriptions

What things and people were like, the setting of a scene.

La maison était grande et il y avait un jardin.The house was big and there was a garden.
Mon grand-père avait une barbe blanche.My grandfather had a white beard.

3. Age, time and weather in the past

J'avais dix ans. Il était huit heures. Il faisait beau.I was ten. It was eight o'clock. The weather was nice.

4. An action in progress

What was going on at a given moment: English \"was -ing\".

À midi, nous mangions sur la plage.At noon, we were eating on the beach.
EnglishFrench
I used to swimje nageais
I would swim (every summer)je nageais
I was swimmingje nageais

Careful with \"would\": only the \"would\" of habit becomes an imparfait (\"Every summer we would go to the sea\" = Tous les étés, on allait à la mer). The other \"would\", as in \"I would like\", is a different tense: je voudrais.

The passé composé and the imparfait work together: the first tells events, the second describes and sets the scene. Choosing between them is the subject of the next lesson.

", "

Holidays at Grandma's in Brittany

Here's how a childhood memory sounds in French. Every verb is in the imparfait, because it's all habits and description:

Quand j'étais petite, je passais tous mes étés chez mes grands-parents, en Bretagne. Ils habitaient une vieille maison près de la mer. Le matin, mon grand-père allait au port et il achetait du poisson. L'après-midi, on allait à la plage avec mes cousins. Il faisait souvent gris, mais on adorait ça !When I was little, I spent every summer at my grandparents' in Brittany. They lived in an old house near the sea. In the morning, my grandfather would go to the harbor and buy fish. In the afternoon, we'd go to the beach with my cousins. It was often gray, but we loved it!

Words that call for the imparfait

FrenchEnglish
quand j'étais petit / petitewhen I was little
quand j'étais enfantwhen I was a child
autrefois, avantin the past, before
d'habitudeusually
souvent, toujoursoften, always
tous les étés, tous les joursevery summer, every day
le dimanche, le mercredion Sundays, on Wednesdays

Then and now

The imparfait is perfect for comparing the past with the present:

Avant, j'habitais à Brest ; maintenant, j'habite à Paris.I used to live in Brest; now I live in Paris.
Avant, il n'y avait pas de téléphone portable.In the past, there were no cell phones.

Il y avait is the imparfait of il y a: there was, there were. It's one of the most useful forms for describing the past.
